reasons: Both texts carry the same saying: a rebuke of treating children by pressing the throat, the instruction to use the Indian aloeswood, and the statement that it holds seven cures including pleurisy.
The wording differs slightly (علامه / علام, بهذا العلاق / بهذه العلائق), A adds a narrative opening and a closing clause on how the remedy is applied, and B adds a gloss naming the wood.

evidence.quote: علامه تدغرن أولادكن بهذا العلاق عليكن بهذا العود الهندي فإن فيه سبعة أشفية منها ذات الجنب
علام تدغرن أولادكن بهذه العلائق عليكن بهذا العود الهندي يعني الكست فإن فيه سبعة أشفية منها ذات الجنب

verdicts.uncertainty_note: B is a bare matn without frame or speaker; if its context showed a different speaker or occasion the reading could shift, but the wording overlap is close.

proposals.text: A adds the method of use: يسعط من العذرة ويلد من ذات الجنب (given as snuff for throat inflammation and by the side of the mouth for pleurisy); B lacks this.
B adds the gloss يعني الكست identifying the Indian wood; A lacks it.
A opens with a narrator's account (a woman bringing her son whose throat had been pressed), which sets the occasion; B has no frame.

reasons: Both describe the same act in nearly identical words: when seated in prayer, hands on knees, raising the finger next to the thumb to supplicate, the left hand spread on the knee.
B specifies the right finger (إصبعه اليمنى) and uses the present tense فيدعو where A has فدعا; otherwise the matn is the same.

evidence.quote: كان إذا جلس في الصلاة وضع يديه على ركبتيه ورفع أصبعه التي تلي الإبهام فدعا بها ويده اليسرى على ركبته باسطها عليها
كان إذا جلس في الصلاة وضع يديه على ركبتيه ورفع إصبعه اليمنى التي تلي الإبهام فيدعو بها واليسرى على ركبته باسطها عليها

verdicts.uncertainty_note: Little would change this; the only question is whether the added اليمنى makes it a variant rather than the same words.

proposals.text: B states explicitly that the raised finger is on the right hand (إصبعه اليمنى); A leaves the hand implicit.

reasons: A is a long exegetical report on the straight path, a story about a man who stole and gave in charity, and a comparison with an interpretation attributed to Mu'awiya; it closes with a saying of the Prophet quoted by al-Sadiq.

B consists only of that closing saying, also attributed to the Prophet, in almost the same words: the bearers of this knowledge in every generation remove from it the distortion of extremists, the false claims of falsifiers and the interpretation of the ignorant.
Nothing else in A corresponds to B, so the correspondence is a quoted passage, not the whole report.

evidence.quote: يحمل هذا العلم من كل خلف عدو له، وينفون عنه تحريف الغالين، وانتحال المبطلين، وتأويل الجاهلين.
يحمل هذا العلم من كل خلف عدو له ينفون عنه تحريف الغالين وانتحال المبطلين وتأويل الجاهلين.

verdicts.uncertainty_note: The shared saying is near-verbatim. A reader treating the claim as about A's whole report would answer differently, since the rest of A has no counterpart in B.

proposals.text: The overlap is confined to the final Prophetic saying in A; the exegesis of اهدنا الصراط المستقيم, the story of the thief, and the Mu'awiya/Ammar passage have no counterpart in B.
In A the saying is quoted by Ja'far al-Sadiq as a closing comment (طوبى للذين هم كما قال رسول الله); in B it is reported through Zayd ibn Ali from his forefathers from Ali as a standalone saying.

reasons: Both list the same assignment of starting points for ihram: Medina from Dhu al-Hulayfa, Syria from al-Juhfa, Najd from Qarn, Yemen from Yalamlam.
B frames it as an answer to a man's question and places the Yemen item outside the quoted words, introduced by ويقولون; A gives all four in one run with مهل.

evidence.quote: مهل أهل المدينة من ذي الحليفة ومهل أهل الشام من الجحفة ومهل أهل نجد من قرن ومهل أهل اليمن من يلملم
يهل أهل المدينة من ذي الحليفة وأهل الشام من الجحفة وأهل نجد من قرن
قال ويقولون وأهل اليمن من يلملم

verdicts.uncertainty_note: A as given has no chain or speaker, so the packet does not show whom A attributes the list to; if A's speaker differed from B's, this could be a same-ruling-different-speaker case. The difference over the Yemen item is also substantive.

proposals.text: In B the Yemen item (Yalamlam) is not within the Prophet's quoted words; the narrator says others report it (قال ويقولون). A states all four, including Yemen, with no such distinction.
B adds the occasion (a man asking من أين نهل) and al-Tirmidhi's closing remarks on parallel reports, grading and practice; A has none of this.

reasons: Both carry the same saying: the speaker was forbidden to recite in bowing and prostration; magnify the Lord in bowing; strive in supplication in prostration, for it is fitting that you be answered.
Wording differs (عن القراءة في الركوع والسجود / أن أقرأ راكعا وساجدا; فأكثروا / فاجتهدوا; فعظموا الله فيه / فعظموا فيه الرب), and A adds a lexical gloss of قمن after the saying.

evidence.quote: إني قد نهيت عن القراءة في الركوع والسجود فأما الركوع فعظموا الله فيه، وأما السجود فأكثروا فيه من الدعاء فإنه قمن أن يستجاب لكم
أَلَا إنِّي نُهِيت أَنْ أَقْرَأَ رَاكِعًا وَسَاجِدًا فَأَمَّا الرُّكُوعُ فَعَظِّمُوا فِيهِ الرَّبَّ وَأَمَّا السُّجُودُ فَاجْتَهَدُوا فِيهِ مِنْ الدُّعَاءِ فَقَمِنَ أَنْ يُسْتَجَابَ لَكُمْ

verdicts.uncertainty_note: B has no stated speaker in the packet; if B were attributed to someone other than the Prophet the reading would become contested, but the first-person نهيت fits the same speaker.

proposals.text: A appends an explanation of the word قمن as meaning جدير وحري (worthy, apt); this is a gloss, not part of the saying, and B lacks it.
A says أكثروا (do much) of supplication in prostration; B says اجتهدوا (strive).

reasons: Both are Zaynab's report from Umm Salama: a woman whose widowed daughter had an eye complaint asks whether she may apply kohl; the answer is no, the waiting period is four months and ten, and in the Jahiliyya a widow threw dung at the year's end.
B adds that the refusal was repeated two or three times; A adds Zaynab's explanation of the Jahiliyya custom and Malik's glosses of تفتض and الحفش.

evidence.quote: إن ابنتي توفي عنها زوجها وقد اشتكت عينها أفأكحلها
إن ابنتي توفي عنها زوجها وقد اشتكت عينها أفتكحلها
إنما هي أربعة أشهر وعشرا وقد كانت إحداكن في الجاهلية ترمي بالبعرة عند رأس الحول
إنما هي أربعة أشهر وعشر، وقد كانت إحداكن في الجاهلية ترمي بالبعرة على رأس الحول

verdicts.uncertainty_note: The shared matn is near-verbatim; only a damaged or misassigned text would change this.

proposals.text: B records that the Prophet said no two or three times (مرتين أو ثلاثا كل ذلك يقول لا); A has a single no.
A adds Humayd's question and Zaynab's description of the pre-Islamic mourning custom (كانت المرأة إذا توفي عنها زوجها دخلت حفشا), plus Malik's glosses; B ends with the saying.
The mother asks أفأكحلها (may I apply kohl to her) in A and أفتكحلها (may she apply kohl) in B, a difference in who applies it.
